textbookText: vi. Natural Selection: This process actually means ‘differential reproduction’ in which some members of a population produce a large number of progeny while others produce less or none. The organisms which are physically, physiologically and behaviorally better adapted to the surrounding survive and reproduce. The better adapted organisms transfer their successful characters to the upcoming generation. Those who are not well adapted fail to reproduce and die in the process of natural selection. In this way, natural selection leads to the change in allele or gene frequencies.

A. Tick the correct alternative. 1. Which of the following is NOT one of the fundamental postulates of Lamarckism? a. Tendency to increase in size b. Direct environmental influence c. Inheritance of acquired character d. Struggle for existence 2. According to Lamarck, what happens to organs that are used frequently? a. They disappear over time b. They become more developed c. They remain unchanged d. They develop defects 3. Which experiment provided strong evidence against the inheritance of acquired characteristics? a. Miller-Urey Experiment b. Weismann's Tailless Mice Experiment c. Louis Pasteur’s experiment d. Evidences from embryology 4. Which of the following is NOT one of the five fundamental facts of Darwinism? a. Enormous fertility b. Survival of the fittest c. Struggle for existence d. Use and disuse of organs 5. What process describes the change in gene frequencies in a population randomly by chance, not due to natural selection? a. Mutation b. Genetic recombination c. Gene migration d. Genetic drift 6. Which type of isolation occurs when a population is divided into separate groups by geographical barriers? a. Reproductive isolation b. Postmating isolation c. Geographical isolation d.
